ops.title: Worker startup dies un-logged in worker_log_key when its root was deleted underneath it
ops.description:
captain_hook/worker/__main__.py:45 — worker_log_key(build) calls os.getcwd(), which raises FileNotFoundError when the worker's root was deleted under it (scratch checkouts, worktrees, TMPDIR roots). It fires BEFORE configure_daemon_logging, so the worker dies un-logged and the daemon pays a full respawn with no attributable error.

Confirmed live in ~/Library/Caches/captain-hook/host-v1/capt-hookd.log on 2026-09-02: repeated tracebacks through daemon/registry.py:180 _build -> configure_daemon_logging(worker_log_key(build)), from 12.22.3 workers. Log is 11.9MB, nearly all stack traces.

Originally surfaced as finding #10 of the 2026-09-02 capt-hook performance audit (~27 hits at the time). Out of scope for PR #32 (dispatch budget + roster gate), filed so it is not lost.

Related standing issue on this host, worth checking together: host and client were build-fence mismatched (helper 12.23.4 vs uv-tool client 12.22.5), and ~/.daemonkit/tools/capt-hook retained 8 versions at 2.0GB with no GC.

ops.text: worker startup survives a deleted cwd, or fails with a logged, attributable error
the failure is logged: it must not fire before configure_daemon_logging
